title: Linux Logging Stack: Journald, Rsyslog, Central Logs

scenes.line1: How do you handle logs from 500 servers?
scenes.say: Ever wonder how you keep track of logs from hundreds of Linux servers? Why bother with central logs anyway?

scenes.label: journald
scenes.sub: Captures logs from services and the kernel.
scenes.say: Journald grabs logs from every service and the kernel, storing them in a structured format.

scenes.label: rsyslog
scenes.sub: Writes classic text files, forwards logs out.
scenes.say: Rsyslog takes those logs and writes them to classic text files, like messages or auth logs. It can also send logs to a central system.
Central log systems like Splunk, ELK, Loki, or Azure Monitor let you search and analyze logs from all your servers in one place.

scenes.title: Send logs to a central server
scenes.say: To forward logs, set up rsyslog with a central server address, restart rsyslog, and test with a logger command.

scenes.question: Why not just keep logs local?
scenes.right: Servers can die, attackers can wipe logs, and you need to search across all hosts for incidents.
scenes.say: Why not keep logs local? Because servers can die, attackers can wipe logs, and you need to search across all hosts during an incident.
